svg.title: Why the model never names a product. The language model plans in ingredient space only: it returns canonical ingredient keys and quantities, such as chicken 400 g, onion 2 pieces, curd 150 g, saffron 1. Deterministic code maps those keys onto the catalogue and decides the product, brand, pack size, pack count, price and stock. So the model cannot hallucinate a product that does not exist, cannot invent a price, and cannot recommend something out of stock. The feature degrades cleanly: with OPENROUTER_API_KEY set, planning is done by the model and the plan header reads AI plan. Without a key it reads Blinkit plan, a built in recipe knowledge base and rule based intent parsing take over, and every screen still works end to end. The app never claims to have used a model it did not.

section.h2: The model never names a product
section.p: The LLM plans in ingredient space. Deterministic code owns the shelf. The only contract between them is a list of canonical ingredient keys on every product.

div.div: No phantom productsIt cannot hallucinate an item that does not exist.
No made up pricesEvery rupee comes from the catalogue.
No dead linksIt cannot recommend something out of stock.

div.span: With OPENROUTER_API_KEY set, the model plans the meal and the header says so.
No key: a built in recipe knowledge base and rule based intent parsing run, and every screen still works. It never claims a model it did not use.
